description: A piano keyboard played with the pointer or with the computer keys, several notes at a time, that hands the model the wave of the chord it is holding.

parameters.label: Wave
parameters.description: A name the model leaves free: the piano works the sound of the chord it is holding out over a window of samples and hands it to the model under that name, defined over sample indices as y\left[n\right]=... is, so it can be plotted, read one sample at a time and superposed with another wave. Sample n is the sum, over every key being held, of its own sine. Left empty, the piano keeps its wave to itself.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: Amplitude of each note in the sum, so a chord of three notes reaches three times this far where they agree.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: How many samples the published wave holds, and so how far its index runs: y\left[1\right] is the wave at the start of the window and y\left[samples\right] the wave at the end of it.

parameters.label: Duration
parameters.description: Seconds of sound the samples span. Two hundredths of a second is about five cycles of middle C, which is enough of the wave to see its shape.

parameters.label: First octave
parameters.description: Octave of the leftmost key. Four starts the keyboard at middle C.

parameters.label: Notes held
parameters.description: The notes the piano is holding, kept while the board is open. It is what draws a key lit and what the wave is summed over, and it is never written down: a file remembers no note left sounding.
